extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in patent analytics, NLP, and machine learning
extracted.subtask_short: patent analysis using texts and images
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for using patent texts, metadata, and drawings/images in automated patent analysis (classification, retrieval, novelty detection, etc.). Discusses strengths, limitations, and empirical performance of text-only, image-only, and hybrid approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata content and utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata typically includes citations/references, classification codes, inventors, applicants, assignees, law firms, and examiners. Researchers have exploited the relationship information between patents through citations and classification codes based on graph neural networks (GNNs) for patent classification and patent valuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use metadata to provide high-level relationship information (e.g., citation graphs, classification-based relations) and to feed graph-based models (GNNs). Metadata is valuable for capturing relationships between patents and for many downstream tasks, but should be understood as complementary to textual content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and limits of classification codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Solely relying on classification codes can sometimes be misleading and become a problem because patents may span multiple technology areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat public classification codes as definitive labels; they are often coarse relative to the number of documents and coarser than internal office classifications. Methods should account for cross-domain patents and potential misclassification if relying only on codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata granularity vs invention detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Importantly, metadata provide high-level information but do typically not include details of the invention, which limits the possibility of capturing the invention and certainly not technical nuances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the goal is to capture technical content or fine-grained novelty, supplement metadata with full-text analysis; metadata alone is insufficient for capturing invention-level technical nuances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image content constraints and formal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In most patent offices, the drawings are not supposed to contain (significant) text beyond reference numbers. The drawings are not helpful for automated processing in many cases. Methods are commonly illustrated as block diagrams, but these diagrams, without supplementary text beyond reference numbers—which many patent offices do not accept for formal reasons—become ambiguous and could be interpreted as representing completely different and undeniably novel inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious when using drawings as sole evidence of technical content. Formal rules limiting text in drawings create ambiguity; image interpretation should be cross-checked with textual disclosure to avoid misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image representation complexity (CAD vs sketches)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent figures from computer aided design (CAD) models may be harder to match with corresponding ones from other documents due to the high number of lines representing details, which tend to overwhelm convolutional neural networks. However, many patents and patent applications contain simpler sketches and schematic figures with the intention to not disclosing more than necessary. Such simplifications can be beneficial for processing with artificial intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the type of drawing: CAD-heavy detailed figures may reduce model performance, while simpler schematic sketches are often easier for CNNs to process. Consider preprocessing, simplification, or feature engineering to handle dense CAD drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image quality and resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Some patent images suffer from low resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low-resolution figures reduce the effectiveness of image-based models. Ensure image quality, perform resolution enhancement when possible, or deprioritize image-only methods on low-quality corpora.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of image-only patent classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Images can serve for automated patent classification. Jiang et al. designed a method based on convolutional neural networks for patent classification using only images and achieved 54.32% accuracy on eight-class prediction. The results are poorer than text-based methods for two main reasons. Firstly, predicting the subject class based solely on images is inherently challenging, even for human experts. Secondly, some patent images suffer from low resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect image-only classification to underperform text-based approaches; empirical evidence (e.g., ~54% accuracy on 8 classes) shows limitations. Use image-only baselines cautiously and benchmark against text-based and multimodal baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of hybrid / multimodal methods
rubrics_metrics.description: By now, researchers have applied convolutional neural networks in patent subject classification and patent retrieval. However, considering the above, the performance of patent classification based on images only appears to be much worse than using texts. Therefore, hybrid methods that leverage multiple sources for patent analysis, such as texts, images, and classification codes, appear promising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine text, metadata, and image modalities where possible: hybrid methods typically outperform unimodal (image-only) approaches. Design multimodal architectures or ensemble approaches to exploit complementary signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalability and prior-art search challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: The size and rapid growth of patent descriptions (including applications that are not granted) and the scientific-technical literature worldwide pose significant challenges to the prior-art search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design methods with scalability in mind (indexing, efficient retrieval, approximate nearest neighbor, long-context models). Be aware that corpus growth increases false negatives/positives in prior-art search and demands efficient, large-scale retrieval strategies.
